nodes.description: Public mapping (address => uint) tracking each hodler's deposited balance
Constant timestamp (1749995999) used as the unlock time for withdrawals
Payable fallback function that credits msg.value to hodlers[msg.sender] and emits Hodl
Withdrawal function gated by block.timestamp > partyTime and a positive hodler balance
msg.sender: caller-controlled address used as mapping key and transfer recipient
block.timestamp: miner-influenceable time used to gate the party() withdrawal
Unchecked += arithmetic on hodlers[msg.sender] += msg.value (Solidity 0.4.12, no SafeMath)
msg.sender.transfer(value) external value transfer that can trigger a callback (reentrancy)
Local variable holding the cached hodler balance before the external transfer

edges.reason: msg.sender is used as the mapping key when crediting hodlers[msg.sender] in the fallback
msg.sender indexes the state slot involved in the unchecked ++/+= arithmetic
Result of the unchecked addition is written back into hodlers[msg.sender], allowing balance overflow
block.timestamp is compared against partyTime and controls whether party() may execute
hodlers[msg.sender] is read into the local variable value inside party()
Local value is passed as the amount of the external msg.sender.transfer call
msg.sender is the recipient of the external transfer, giving the caller control during the call
party() execution reaches the external msg.sender.transfer(value) call
The payable fallback path mutates hodlers[msg.sender] on every deposit
The external transfer can re-enter the payable fallback and re-credit hodlers before state settles

normalization_plan.reason: The local variable value is only a temporary alias for the amount passed to the external transfer operation, so it can be folded into that unsafe_operation node
